sections.history: Therazhundur, the Thiruvazhundur of the hymns, is one of the 108 Divya Desams and one of the shrines of Chola Nadu, a village near Kuthalam in the Mayiladuthurai country. Thirumangai Alvar sang its lord at length in the Periya Thirumozhi — tradition counts forty-five of his verses here, among the most he gave any shrine. Tradition holds that the temple was first raised by the early Chola king Karikala, and later centuries added to it. The village is honoured too as the birthplace of Kambar, the poet of the Tamil Ramayana, so that Therazhundur stands in the memory of Tamil devotion and Tamil letters alike.
sections.architecture: Built in the Dravidian manner, the temple enshrines Devadirajan standing and facing east beneath the Garuda Vimanam; uniquely, Garuda stands beside the lord within the sanctum. The festival image, Amaruviappan, stands with his consorts and with a cow and calf at his side, and the Goddess Sengamalavalli has her own shrine. The Darshana Pushkarini lies before the temple, outside the main entrance.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells that Brahma, to test Krishna, hid away the cows of the cowherd village, and Krishna simply made new herds. Abashed, Brahma begged forgiveness and asked the lord to appear here, and he came as Amaruviappan, the cowherd with cow and calf. Tradition also holds that the Kaveri did penance here to be freed from the curse of the sage Agastya.
sections.festivals: The Brahmotsavam is held in the Tamil month of Vaikasi; Andal's festival is kept in Aadi, and Thirumangai Alvar's festival and the festival of lamps in Karthigai. In Thai the lord rides out on Garuda, and Vaikunta Ekadashi is kept with devotion.
sections.experience: A village temple of unhurried calm, Therazhundur rewards the pilgrim who comes to see Amaruviappan with cow and calf, and Garuda standing within the sanctum. Visitors who love Tamil literature will want to remember Kambar here; the Darshana Pushkarini before the gate is a quiet place to sit.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; the Vaikasi Brahmotsavam and Vaikunta Ekadashi are busiest. Confirm current timings before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Therazhundur lies near Kuthalam, about 10 km west of Mayiladuthurai, reachable by road; Mayiladuthurai Junction and Kuthalam are the nearest railway stations, and Tiruchirappalli the nearest airport.
